# linux_block_devices (Data Source)

Lists the disks, partitions and other block devices of the host, as `lsblk` reports them. Device names such as `/dev/sdb` depend on the order disks were found: select disks by `serial`, `wwn` or size, or as the disk that is not `root_disk`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A data volume attached after the host started: wait for it, then take
# the only disk that does not hold the root file system.
data "linux_block_devices" "all" {
  wait_for_disks = 2
}

locals {
  data_disk = one([
    for d in data.linux_block_devices.all.devices : d.path
    if d.type == "disk" && d.path != data.linux_block_devices.all.root_disk
  ])
}

# Or select a disk by its serial number, which often holds the volume ID on
# cloud providers.
output "volume" {
  value = [for d in data.linux_block_devices.all.devices : d.path if d.serial == "vol0abc123"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `wait_for_disks` (Number) Wait until the host has at least this many disks, for instance for a volume attached after the host started.
- `wait_timeout` (String) Maximum time to wait for `wait_for_disks`, as a Go duration such as `5m`. Defaults to `5m`.

### Read-Only

- `devices` (Attributes List) Block devices, disks followed by what they hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--devices))
- `id` (String) Always `block_devices`.
- `root_disk` (String) Disk holding the root file system, such as `/dev/sda`, through partitions, LVM or RAID. Empty when it cannot be told, for instance in a container.

<a id="nestedatt--devices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `devices`

Read-Only:

- `fstype` (String) Type of the file system or signature, such as `ext4`, `swap` or `LVM2_member`.
- `kernel_name` (String) Kernel name, such as `nvme1n1` or `dm-0`.
- `label` (String) Label of the file system.
- `model` (String) Disk model.
- `mountpoint` (String) Where the device is mounted.
- `parent` (String) Path of the device holding this one, such as the disk of a partition.
- `partlabel` (String) Name of the GPT partition.
- `partuuid` (String) UUID of the partition.
- `path` (String) Device path, such as `/dev/nvme1n1` or `/dev/mapper/vg-data`.
- `read_only` (Boolean) Whether the device is read-only.
- `serial` (String) Disk serial number. On cloud providers, it often holds the volume ID.
- `size` (Number) Size in bytes.
- `type` (String) `disk`, `part`, `lvm`, `crypt`, `raid1`, `loop`, `rom`...
- `uuid` (String) UUID of the file system.
- `wwn` (String) World Wide Name of the disk.
